title: Open scalar comparison with unit, tensor and composition normalization
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $A\to B$ a map of finite commutative rings. On ordinary unbounded constant-ring pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $U_T$ be scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and use the scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Use exact open adjunctions $j_!^R\dashv j_R^{-1}$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] and the canonical $\lambda_j:j_B^{-1}S_X\cong S_Uj_A^{-1}$ [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The common-right-adjoint comparison defines a B-linear natural isomorphism $\beta_j:S_Xj_!^A\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^BS_U$. Its inverse is the open adjunct of $\lambda_j^{-1}\circ S_U(\eta_j^A)$. Under scalar restriction and the canonical tensor identifications, beta is the open projection isomorphism at the constant module B [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. For $A\to B\to C$, these beta maps compose to beta for $A\to C$ under balanced scalar associativity [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], including identities.

For arbitrary $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $Q\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ let $\gamma^R$ be the forward open projection isomorphism $(j_!^RM)\otimes_R^LN\to j_!^R(M\otimes_R^Lj_R^{-1}N)$. The following two routes from $S_X(j_!^AK\otimes_A^LQ)$ to $j_!^B(S_UK\otimes_B^Lj_B^{-1}S_XQ)$ agree: (i) $S_X\gamma^A$, then $\beta_{j,K\otimes j_A^{-1}Q}$, then $j_!^B$ of the scalar monoidal comparison and $\lambda_j^{-1}$; (ii) the scalar monoidal comparison, then $\beta_{j,K}\otimes1$, then $\gamma^B$. Thus beta preserves the unit-normalized open tensor map, for arbitrary Q.

proof.text: Obtain canonical scalar and tensor presentations, normalized open monoidal choices, scalar projection invertibility and the inverse tensor compatibility equation.

Construct the inverse projection by transposing the natural map given by the open unit tensor identity followed by the inverse restriction tensorator. Naturality follows from unit and tensorator naturality. Instantiate PurCompactSupport.openProjectionInverse_isIso with the constant-ring coefficient system and tensorModel m to get componentwise invertibility; assemble the natural isomorphism. Its inverse adjunct is the Hom equivalence inverse law. Then obtain its scalar-restriction interpretation. Also obtain the coefficient composition and identity equations for inverse lambda, before taking any open adjunct.

Expand composite adjunction units in the common-right-adjoint definition of beta. Scalar unit naturality and the defining mate equation identify the open adjunct of beta inverse with scalar extension of the open unit followed by lambda inverse. Transport across scalarIso by naturality. This is scalarOpenTranspose, transported_open_unit and beta_inverse_aux in Lean.

For coefficient composition, compare inverse beta routes after postcomposition by the scalar associator and applying the open C Hom bijection. Move the open unit across the inverse scalar associator, substitute the inverse beta adjunct twice, and use naturality of inverse lambda to combine the two open B maps. The inverse-lambda coefficient cocycle replaces the remaining three maps. Naturality of the scalar associator at the open unit then cancels that associator and its inverse, leaving exactly the composite-coefficient inverse beta adjunct. Invert the equality of isomorphisms. For the identity coefficient map, the same argument uses the inverse-lambda identity equation and scalar unitor naturality. These are the complete private coefficient_comp and coefficient_id calculations in Lean.

Compare the inverse tensor-square routes using the open B Hom bijection. Move the open unit across the first route by naturality, substitute beta_inverse, move inverse lambda across inverse projection, and substitute the inverse projection adjunct. Tensorator naturality then moves the open unit through the inverse scalar tensorator. The inverse lambda tensor equation identifies the remaining composites, after which lambda at Q cancels. On the other route substitute beta_inverse at K and the B inverse projection adjunct. Naturality of the B inverse restriction tensorator gives exactly the same adjunct. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence, then inversion of the resulting isomorphism equality, proves the forward tensor square for arbitrary K,Q. This is the complete private tensor_square proof in Lean.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-774ae5681 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 15 cited statements in full; there are no new nodes and no fixes. Against N0's base copy, the statement changes only by adding [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to the λ_j citation and to stmt_deps; it is not weakened. No SGA source, no cycle (item absent from the 2929-node dep closure), and no re-split note. Steps 1–8 re-derived with all directions written out. (1) λ^{-1} is the scalar mate of r_A U_X = U_U r_B (K-flat node), so ν_U = U_U(λ) r_A ν_X; λ is monoidal as c'∘c^{-1} of the two ringed-topos factorisations of (U,B)→(X,A) (monoidal-comparisons node). (2–3) The conjugate lemma applies with L1 = S_X e_A, L2 = e_B S_U. Composite units plus scalar-unit naturality give (*): r_B(b) u^B = λ^{-1} S_U(u^A). (4) (**) matches the Yoneda chain of Stacks 0E8I (sites-modules l.4051), the projection-formula node's imported proof, and the reviewed lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization. Advisory only: the step reads which canonical map is meant from the source. (5) U_X b = δ^A_{K,B_X} follows from the restriction/extension identification and the tensorator a_A. (6) The cocycle follows by pasting conjugates, then the successive-quotient units and uniqueness; the identity case works. (7–8) (***) is exactly the inverse of routes (i)/(ii). (J) and the left-side reduction agree after using λ-monoidality as t_U S_U(a_A) λ = (λ⊗λ) a_B r_B(t_X); no symmetry is used, so no sign. Edge cases checked: U empty, j = id, A = B, Q = A, the nonflat map Z/4→Z/2. Tool uses (8 generic comparison and adjunction nodes; unit uses = []) accepted. Maintainer note: the β existence/inverse clause, which was already in N0's base statement, overlaps the reviewed lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization (g = id). That node lacks the restricted-β, cocycle and mixed-square clauses, so this delivery has no fault there. lem-sp-proetale-open-scalar-cocycle is a special case (ℓ-power rings), not a duplicate.
